verdict.rationale: Foreloop documents connecting GitHub so it can read your code and so an agent can open pull requests. Agent access is then set up with a few lightweight steps: a global npm install, `foreloop init` in the checkout, and an MCP URL plus an API key. That is relatively simple, but it is a multi-step setup rather than a documented one-click install. missing for 10: a documented one-click repository install/authorization flow (e.g. GitHub App install), details of the GitHub connection steps and permission scoping, independent or hands-on corroboration of setup ease.

support.subject: As a developer, I can grant an agent access to my repositories with a one-click install, without complex setup

citations.quote: Connecting GitHub is how Foreloop reads your code, and how an agent opens a pull request against it.
Connect a repository and get automatic product reviews on your pull requests.
foreloop init installs the task-executor skill into the checkout, which is what teaches an agent working there how to claim and report on Foreloop tasks.
An MCP client needs that URL and an API key and nothing else.
